parts.text: Which claim correctly traces the resources used and a way to reduce unnecessary use or pollution?

options.text: The bath uses water directly and coal-based electricity indirectly; a shorter shower uses less of both and can cut pollution.
Stop washing altogether because all washing wastes water.
A bath uses only water; electricity and coal are not linked to this activity, even indirectly.
Clear hot water cannot involve air pollution, so no pollution-reduction action is needed.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

stem: Yusuf runs a bath with tap water heated by electricity from a power plant that burns coal.

part_answers.answer: The bath uses water and, through electricity, coal; using less hot water reduces both resource use and related pollution.

teacher.key_rationale: Trace direct water use and indirect coal-electricity use, then reduce unnecessary use. Stopping all washing, denying indirect coal use, or judging by clear water alone miss that hinge.
